questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that an obstacle is ahead, such as a traffic island or barrier. You must drive to the right of it.

questions.question: The most common mistake when backing up is not looking both ways behind the car.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Most drivers back up without looking in all directions. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window to see more.

questions.question: Yield means you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you also must stop if it is not safe to merge into the flow of traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that an intersection with another road is coming ahead.

questions.question: On long trips, you can stop feeling drowsy by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping often to rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips to prevent drowsiness. Stop and rest often, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
Drivers check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yield the right-of-way.
Drivers keep a four-second distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes occur when drivers speed for the conditions. Always follow the speed limit and drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always use your signal, even if no other cars are visible.
Signal only if you see other cars.
Signal only at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your signal, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or leaving a curb. Make signaling a habit so you always follow the law.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal for any movement left or right. Signal when changing lanes, leaving a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you see unexpected movements from other drivers.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop for unexpected events.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Drive only on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to lower your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra distance from that vehicle.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Do not talk to passengers, search your vehicle, read, sightsee, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, stay far away. They are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: What can happen when you combine alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects much stronger. For example, one drink mixed with a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Do not look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow closely behind them.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm when dealing with an aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Create as much distance as possible between you and them. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let other cars pass.
Can create a dangerous situation.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is hazardous. On a two-lane road, if cars are backing up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to your exit.
Stop a police officer and ask them to help you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. Do not swerve across lanes to make an exit at the last second. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Go through turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, driving too fast is especially dangerous in turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when taking turns in bad conditions.

questions.question: Cell phones are a serious source of driver distraction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: While driving, do not use cell phones, computers, or other devices. Only use them to report a crash or emergency. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: A tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the wheel straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and drive straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slowly release the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control of the car. When it is safe, brake gently and pull off the road.

questions.question: An officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other drivers are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help traffic move safely. Drivers must obey traffic signals. However, when an officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: Driving well below the speed limit is:

options.text: Optional.
Smart.
Safe.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Unless road or weather conditions require it, driving well below the speed limit is dangerous. Slow drivers force other drivers to take risky actions to pass.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right side of the road and let it pass?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or sirens, you must pull to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: What should you do before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb?

options.text: Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal before you move. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Signal only while you are making the move, not before.
You do not need to signal if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you move. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What is important to know about trucks on the road?

options.text: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Trucks pass other vehicles faster when going downhill.
Trucks turn in a smaller space than smaller vehicles.
Trucks pass other vehicles faster when going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: Does smoking while driving affect your driving?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving abilities.
No, it helps keep the driver alert.
Yes, it is a distraction.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. It can cause you to take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly go under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Can you text while driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, anytime in any way.
Yes, if you are a very skilled driver.
Yes, if you only look away for a moment.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal. You cannot use a cell phone or device to send, read, or write text messages while driving. You also cannot use handheld devices for voice calls while driving unless you use a hands-free device.

questions.question: What should you do if you see water covering the road?

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through because the water is unlikely to be too deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded roads. Turn around and find another way. You cannot tell how deep the water is or how strong the current is. Your vehicle could be swept away or submerged.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tire tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a layer of water on the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Is it illegal to leave a child under eight alone in a vehicle if conditions are unsafe?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never leave a child under eight alone in a vehicle if it is unsafe. A person at least 12 years old must supervise the child at all times.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way to drive around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning sign.
